correctness.rationale: Exact invariant line-space support-interval derivation establishes the normalization and piecewise formula. Independent sector quadrature and rejection sampling agree in all tested cases. Direct derivatives give C1 matching, inradius curvature jump and circumradius three-halves asymptotic; finite tests supplement rather than substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons with the two central 2009/2012 invariant-line regular-polygon chord-length papers found the same sampling measure but different marginals (chord lengths and random point-pair distances). Neither states or implies the full offset-from-center probability and strict all-n order from their claimed marginal results. General Cauchy-Crofton normalization is attributed, and the order across nonnested polygons was not found in the indexed records. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The observable is a natural conditional Crofton probability for a concentric target. The theorem determines the entire distribution with sharp inradius and circumradius singularities and gives a global strict stochastic ordering across nonnested regular polygons. As a result one exact target-hit probability resolves the discrete side-count inverse problem at fixed scale, a structural geometry classification beyond a single routine integral.
